companyDescription.text:
As Purchasing Business Analyst you are a numbers-minded partner to the purchasing teams, helping them decide better and sooner by turning large data sets into a short list of priorities and realistic options. You place each finding in its business setting, spell out the trade-offs, and see to it that analysis ends in decisions people act on and better routines. 

You work with several teams and categories to agree on common definitions and data quality, so that results can be compared and lessons shared. Through good relationships and honest questions, you lead across teams without a formal mandate and step outside your own scope when it helps. 

You succeed in this role by: making data into clear priorities, getting people behind decisions, and changing how we work in ways that last and scale.

jobDescription.text:
Among the things you will lead: 

  • Track KPI/APL results, point out deviations and trends, and turn them into concrete actions and decision points. 

  • Build a common data foundation across teams and categories (definitions, data quality, comparability) so the figures we steer by can be trusted. 

  • Prepare insight for decisions by combining internal and external data (history, trends, benchmarks) and laying out options with their gains, risks and costs. 

  • Help teams work through hard business questions with analysis and good facilitation – deep enough to be sound, light enough to be useful (knowing when it is “enough to decide”). 

  • Bring stakeholders together and follow up until a decision is in place and part of daily work (updated processes, routines and owners). 

  • Support, where it fits, core processes e.g., APL, SDP, PDP, BCPs, RFQs

qualifications.text:
You are curious and analytical, and you lead with data. You can turn large amounts of information into a simple story, choose priorities, and give recommendations people can act on. You build trust, speak plainly and with confidence, and you enjoy shaping decisions with many stakeholders. 

  • Strong analytical skills: frame problems, analyse data, reach conclusions and present findings clearly and convincingly. 

  • Business knowledge from a core function (purchasing, logistics or engineering) and a good grasp of its processes and KPIs. 

  • Able to work across teams and categories to align definitions and data quality and make results comparable. 

  • Influence without a mandate: win support, coach and question constructively, and move people from talk to decision.
